In SCOPe 2.08 all three are sibling families inside the same superfamily, c.2.1 "NAD(P)-binding Rossmann-fold domains" (sunid 51735), which is the sole-named superfamily of fold c.2 (sunid 51734) in class c (alpha and beta, a/b). The superfamily has 12 named families plus an automated-matches family c.2.1.0.

So a biologist should treat ADH C-terminal domains, CoA-binding domains and K+-channel RCK/KTN domains as homologous at the superfamily level: a remote-homology inference, supported by structure and ligand-binding geometry rather than sequence. (2) Family = the stronger claim, and it is NOT shared among them. Membership in a SCOPe family implies clear sequence similarity (typically >=30% identity) or very similar structure and function. These three are different families, so SCOPe is explicitly saying the three groups are only remotely related and have diverged in sequence and function. The ADH family comment even notes that its grouping is defined by the companion N-terminal all-beta (GroES-like, b.35) domain, i.e. family identity rests on whole-protein domain architecture, not just the Rossmann domain. (3) Fold level is weaker still: other c.2 fold members, and the neighbouring folds c.3 (FAD/NAD(P)-binding) and c.4 (nucleotide-binding), share similar nucleotide-binding modes (as the c.2 fold comment states) but SCOPe does not assert homology at the fold level; shared fold alone is never evidence of common ancestry.

Functional divergence and what must not be transferred. The three families bind different ligands and do different jobs: ADH-like C-terminal domains bind NAD(P)+ as a catalytic cofactor for a zinc-dependent oxidoreductase; the CoA-binding domain binds the adenine-nucleotide moiety of coenzyme A in ligases/synthetases (no redox chemistry); the K+-channel RCK/KTN domain binds NAD(H)/nucleotides as a regulatory ligand that gates ion conduction (the Kch RCK domain and MthK do not catalyse a reaction). Therefore: do not transfer enzymatic activity, EC number, catalytic residues, cofactor identity or specificity (NAD vs NADP vs CoA) from one family to another; superfamily co-membership predicts only an adenine-nucleotide binding site at the C-terminal edge of the sheet. Do not transfer domain boundaries: ADH entries are two-domain chains (b.35 + c.2.1.1), succinyl-CoA synthetase alpha chain and the channel proteins have other domains, and the Rossmann segment in each is defined independently.
